newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Grain panel spotlight on Spanish maize imports.
newsitem.headline: Grain panel spotlight on Spanish maize imports.

text.p: Preferential maize imports into Spain will be the main tender item at the weekly meeting of the European Union cereals management committee on Thursday, EU officials said.
The EU has ended other 1996/97 (July/June) grain tenders. It could open tenders for next season at the end of June but is not expected to be in any hurry to grant export licences.
Last week the EU rejected all bids to import maize into Spain at a reduced tariff.
It also reduced the quota, which compensates U.S. exporters for trade losses after Spain joined the EU in 1986, to 550,000 tonnes, from 800,000 tonnes.
The reduction followed an upwards revision in estimated Spanish imports of grain substitutes, such as corn gluten feed.
The committee is due to decide how much subsidised cereals and rice should be sent to the Canary Islands, Madeira and the Azores in 1997/98 (July/June), the officials added.
Cereals and rice shipments to these remote Spanish and Portuguese islands benefit from EU export refunds.
Before the committee meets, EU grain experts will discuss measures to implement a new cumulative recovery system for husked rice, which enters into force on July 1.

The optional system was agreed in April following a U.S. complaint to the World Trade Organisation concerning management of duty-free quotas for 8,000 tonnes of brown rice and 36,000 tonnes of partly processed rice.
"The aim is to ensure that everyone knows and applies the rules," said one official.

The system allows traders to reclaim excess import duty payments made under the EU's representative price system if they can prove these are higher than levels set under the GATT Uruguay Round agreement.
